bull.b: Rising production from operator activity can expand Viper’s royalty revenue without requiring it to operate the wells. The Q3 outlook combines organic growth with Riverbend contributions, while the multi-year development pipeline supports continued volume growth over the next several quarters.

The mineral and royalty model gives Viper exposure to production while shifting drilling, completion, and operating spending to third-party operators. This can support strong operating cash conversion and scalable growth, provided activity continues across its acreage.

A higher base dividend establishes a stronger recurring shareholder return, while the revised framework preserves flexibility to fund acquisitions, reduce debt, or repurchase shares. Downside puts and a stated low dividend breakeven further support distribution resilience.

bear.b: Persistently negative free cash flow means operating inflows are being overwhelmed by investment or other cash outflows. If this continues, Viper may have less flexibility to fund acquisitions, reduce debt, or sustain discretionary shareholder returns internally.

Low and volatile net profitability makes earnings power less dependable than revenue growth alone suggests. The swings reduce confidence that production gains will consistently translate into bottom-line returns and could constrain durable capital allocation during weaker periods.

Royalty cash flows remain exposed to oil and gas prices, while hedges only protect against part of an adverse move and carry costs or limitations. Removing the 75% cash-return commitment also makes total quarterly distributions less predictable.
